text:
maria: FYI nightly long-context eval spike on v2-quantX. Lost-instruction failures jumped ~10x vs last night. Repro below, anyone from eng-runtime free?

ben: Saw the dashboard. Looks like outputs truncate around token ~4096 and drop the final instruction block. Could be KV wrap or off-by-one in seq accounting. :thinking_face: 

sophie: eval-bot: nightly_eval/long_context v2-quantX -> failure_rate=12.3% (baseline v2-raw=0.9%). Regression EV-1423 created: https://redwood/ev/EV-1423 

maria: Repro prompt + generation (cut):
```
PROMPT:
System: You are a helpful assistant.
User: I will paste a long document. After it, please summarize the three key action items and number them.
[LONG DOC ~ 6.5k tokens omitted for brevity]
User: Now, summarize the three key action items and be explicit.

GENERATION (v2-quantX):
1) Consolidate logs and set retention to 90 days.
2) Add metrics.
3) Update infra.

[EXPECTED: a 3-paragraph detailed numbered list referencing specific sections. The generation above stops mid-sentence and misses the final instruction about referencing sections]
```

kai: Can you drop the exact request ID from the failed job? I want to check kv metadata and seqnums in the runtime logs.

maria: Request id: r-0ac3b9f1; attached runtime snippet: 
```
[2026-11-07T03:24:12Z] request=r-0ac3b9f1 seq_start=0 seq_end=4096 kv_index=4096 kv_slot=63
[2026-11-07T03:24:12Z] debug: kv_seqnum=4096 expected_next=4097
[2026-11-07T03:24:12Z] warn: kv_index_wrap at seq 4097 -> evict_prefix=true
[2026-11-07T03:24:12Z] trace: emit_tokens up_to=4096 truncated=true
```

ben: That warn looks suspicious. If kv_index_wrap is triggering eviction mid-response, we can lose the tail of the instruction. Could be that the quantized model uses slightly larger token IDs or different length behavior, pushing the effective context over the limit. But the wrap is a runtime event.

kai: Two quick checks: (1) does tokenization with quantX model change token counts? (2) is batching sometimes concatenating context across requests and pushing seq_end over max_seq? Run this locally with --dump-token-counts and --emit-seq.

maria: Ran token counts: same as raw model for this example (4098 tokens). The request is over the configured max of 4096 by 2 tokens. The weird part is yesterday the same prompt passed. So either rounding changed (quantX) or eviction threshold became inclusive.

ben: Also check continuous-batching boundary logic. I remember a recent change that optimizes batch padding by folding small requests; could cause an off-by-one when combined with prefix eviction.

sophie: eval-bot: queued diagnostic run EV-1423-rt1: v2-quantX + --dump-kv --emit-seq --no-cont-batching across 50 cases. ETA ~ 20m. Link: https://redwood/ev/EV-1423/rt1 

sam: @kai @ben I'm on it. I'll tail the canary cluster logs now. If eviction is triggering incorrectly we should either (A) clamp inputs to 4096 for canary, or (B) make eviction non-destructive until response done. Which do we prefer for a fast mitigation?

kai: Fast mitigation = clamp. Long term = fix off-by-one in eviction policy. Also add an assert in the runtime that refuses to evict while a request is emitting tokens.

maria: For tonight I'll roll back quantX on canary and re-run nightly; want to avoid customer impact. Can someone file a runtime bug with the log snippet and stack? I'll attach EV-1423.

ben: I'll open bug: INF-6619 runtime: kv eviction while emitting response (include snippet). Assign to eng-runtime.

sophie: eval-bot: diagnostic EV-1423-rt1 completed: failure_rate=11.8% on instrumented run (similar). Dump shows kv_eviction events correlate with step where emit_tokens flagged truncated=true.

maria: Thanks. Taking the canary rollback now. Will update EV-1423 with results and a short repro script.

kai: Follow-ups: add unit test for seqnum wrap, add telemetry for kv_eviction cause (manual vs auto vs wrap), and add a guard to avoid eviction during emit.

sam: Watching the rollback now. Ping me if the rollback doesn't reduce failures in next run. :eyes:

maria: Closing loop: rolled back v2-quantX canary at 03:52Z. Next nightly will re-run and I'll post results here. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
